clue.text: Sharpness wins fight — heads are knocked off

indicators.note: the heads of the two words wins and fight are their first letters, and those are knocked off

explanation.surface: A boxer's sharpness wins the bout, with blows to the head knocking opponents out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads are knocked off' removes the W of 'wins' and the F of 'fight', leaving INS and IGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is keen perception or penetration of mind, a mental sharpness.

clue.text: At home and cross after virus's arrival

indicators.note: after says the cross comes behind the virus in the answer

parts.note: at home means in, as in 'staying in'
flu is an illness caused by a virus
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: Someone at home gets cross when a virus arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: An influx is an arrival of people or things in large numbers.

clue.text: Reporter's small bed on base

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a crib is a baby's bed
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A journalist sleeps on a small bed at the army base.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a writer, often used loosely for a journalist.

clue.text: Observer supporting smashing dish

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below, so the observer goes under the other word

parts.note: smashing means very good
a looker is one who looks, an observer

explanation.surface: Someone watches over a smashed dish.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Dish' is slang for an attractive person, which is what a good-looker is.

clue.text: Claw from rabbit cut leg

indicators.note: cut means the end of the word is chopped off

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chattering at length
the leg side in cricket is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A claw was taken from a rabbit with an injured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit as a verb (from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork', talk) means chatter. The leg side of a cricket pitch is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Use penny Oscar kept in wallet

indicators.note: kept in says the first pieces are held inside the wallet

parts.note: a purse is a small wallet for money
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone finds a use for a penny and an Oscar statuette stored in a wallet.
explanation.definitionFit: Purpose and use both mean the function or point of something.

clue.text: Teacher in favour of oil company purchased by father

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: something purchased by someone is held by them, so the company goes inside father

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
Esso is a well-known oil company brand

explanation.surface: A teacher supports an oil company that his father bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor is a senior university teacher.

clue.text: European cutting socialist's grass

indicators.note: cutting means the letter cuts into the middle of the other word

parts.note: red is a common term for a socialist

explanation.surface: A European is mowing the socialist's lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grasses growing in wet ground.

clue.text: Decoration or star, new on top of tree

parts.note: a star is a big name, a celebrity

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A decoration, or a star, is newly put on top of the Christmas tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is something used for decoration, such as a bauble.

clue.text: Male's been swimming without a costume

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters move about freely into a new order
without says the letter a is taken out of the mixed letters

explanation.surface: A man has been skinny-dipping, swimming without a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of MALESBEEN, minus A, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a matching outfit of clothes, a costume.

clue.text: Sacrifice in the place of god, mainly

parts.note: for can mean instead of, as in 'a substitute for'

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A sacrifice is offered in a temple, mostly to a god.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to give it up, to sacrifice it.

clue.text: Learner doctor does one's unfinished jobs

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A trainee doctor handles one's leftover tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose ends are details still to be tidied up or completed.

clue.text: Not just nuts

explanation.surface: Not just nuts, but something more.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both lacking fairness or balance and mentally disturbed.

clue.text: One leads in mosque, aiding Muslims

definitions.text: One leads in mosque, aiding Muslims

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: the leads in the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Describes a figure who leads prayers in a mosque, helping the faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads the prayers in a mosque, so the whole clue describes him.

clue.text: Choose Dickens character, e.g. The Artful Dodger

parts.note: to pick is to choose
Herbert Pocket is a character in Dickens's Great Expectations

explanation.surface: Pick a Dickens character, such as the Artful Dodger.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Dodger is the Dickens character wanted; he is the definition, a young thief in Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Artful Dodger is a boy thief in Oliver Twist who steals from people's pockets.

clue.text: False coin son forged — father may hear about it here

definitions.text: father may hear about it here

indicators.note: forged means faked or made anew, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A son forged a coin, and the priest may hear all about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic priest, called Father, hears confessions in a booth in church.

clue.text: Encouraging shot — golfer isn't losing length

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are jumbled
losing says a letter is taken away from the mixture

explanation.surface: An encouraging shot shows the golfer isn't losing distance off the tee.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: GOLFERISNT minus L is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Fostering means promoting or nurturing development, so encouraging it.

clue.text: Seal of approval consequently keeping medic excited

indicators.note: keeping says the medic is held inside the other word

parts.note: thus means therefore, consequently
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine
up means excited, as in 'het up'

explanation.surface: An excited doctor gives a seal of approval as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised thumb gesture signals approval or agreement.

clue.text: German writer embraced by French one finally squeezed without hands

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside the French word

parts.note: une is French for one (feminine)
Thomas Mann was a German novelist

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A German author is hugged so tightly by a Frenchwoman he is left without hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' here means crew or workers, as in 'all hands on deck'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that is unmanned has no crew, no hands aboard.

clue.text: Stir fast?

parts.note: stir is slang for prison, and a fast is refusal of food: a protest by starving in jail

explanation.surface: Stir something quickly, as in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' reads as a cooking verb and 'fast' as quickly; instead 'stir' is British slang for prison and 'fast' a noun, a prisoner's refusal of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners have used refusal of food as protest, a famous form of jail fast.

clue.text: Worship continually in Religious Education

indicators.note: in says the first word goes inside the other

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
ever means always, continually

explanation.surface: Pupils worship constantly in their Religious Education lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to hold in deep respect or adoration.

clue.text: Nervous about my boss, for example, getting upset

parts.note: on means about, concerning
for a journalist or setter, the boss is the editor, ED

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is nervous about their boss, who gets angry.
explanation.definitionFit: On edge means tense, jumpy and anxious.

clue.text: Lamb perhaps satisfied penning fourth of essays

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as sheep in a pen

parts.note: met means satisfied, as in 'met the requirements'

indicators.note: the fourth of a word is its fourth letter

explanation.surface: Charles Lamb was satisfied writing his essays.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Charles Lamb, the English essayist; the definition is lamb the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb is an example of meat, the flesh of a young sheep.

clue.text: These words could make gent vamoose, possibly, with seconds to go

definitions.text: These words could make gent vamoose, possibly, with seconds to go

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged another way
to go says the letter for seconds is removed

explanation.surface: An order to hurry could make a man leave sharpish.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: GENTVAMOOSE minus S is rearranged; the phrase also is just what would make someone vamoose.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an urging to hurry up and leave.

clue.text: Superior to Raab, overrules Houses

indicators.note: Houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Dominic Raab, a British politician, thinks himself superior and overrules Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Superior' alone as the definition; 'superior to' swaps for the preposition, while 'superior' alone does not.
explanation.definitionFit: To be above something is to rank higher than it.

clue.text: African country miles north of a large island

indicators.note: in a down clue north of means placed above

explanation.surface: An African country lies miles north of a big island.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Romanians touring small country

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the letters roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Romanian tourists visit a tiny country.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny republic within Italy, among Europe's smallest states.

clue.text: Massage skin regularly each day

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Massage the skin regularly every day.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work muscles with the hands, as in a massage.

clue.text: Turning up with diamonds and ring — that's sweet

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned round, so it reads backwards

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit
ding is the ringing sound of a bell

explanation.surface: Someone turns up with diamonds and an engagement ring, which is sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain 'sweet' is a dessert, and a pudding is the same course.

clue.text: Radical former lover getting married in plane?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the tree

parts.note: a plane is a kind of tree

explanation.surface: An ex-partner gets married on an aeroplane, a drastic step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft; it is the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme and radical both describe views or measures far from the norm.
